page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server instance configured with 12 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory. The underlying hardware features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz across 12 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. This instance integrates two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this server type, meaning storage resources must be attached externally.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10% tier. Multi-core performance, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, falls within the average middle 50% tier, reflecting the 12-vCPU limit. Memory performance is robust, with large-block read and write bandwidth tests scoring in the top 25% tier. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing, while LLM inference benchmarks show top 10% speeds for small model text generation and top 25% speeds for medium model text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high GPU resource density relative to its moderate CPU core count, making it a specialized option for workloads that require substantial VRAM and parallel processing power without needing massive multi-core CPU scaling. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, which requires external volume provisioning. This server is suited for machine learning inference, small to medium LLM execution, image processing, and GPU-accelerated graphics rendering or ray tracing.
